economy.summary: Opposes the Trump administration's tariffs, saying they act as taxes on American consumers and will raise prices on groceries, cars, electronics, and fuel. Hosted a 2026 field hearing in Collegeville on the cost-of-living crisis.
economy.short: Opposes tariffs she says raise consumer prices for families.

taxes.summary: Voted against the 2025 Republican tax-and-spending reconciliation bill (H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill), saying it cuts Medicaid and SNAP to fund tax benefits for the wealthiest Americans.
taxes.short: Voted against 2025 tax bill, citing Medicaid and SNAP cuts.

abortion.summary: Cosponsors the Women's Health Protection Act of 2025 (H.R. 12), which would establish a federal statutory right to abortion access and bar state restrictions on pre-viability abortion.
abortion.short: Cosponsors bill establishing federal right to abortion access.

education.summary: A former professor, she says on her campaign site that quality education is the key to a successful future and lists strong education systems among her core priorities.
education.short: Says quality education is key; prioritizes strong education systems.

healthcare.summary: Says every person has a right to affordable, accessible, quality healthcare. Voted against the 2025 reconciliation bill, saying she would not vote to strip healthcare from 17 million Americans, including more than 300,000 Pennsylvanians.
healthcare.short: Supports healthcare as a right; opposed bill cutting Medicaid coverage.

energy.summary: Advocates moving toward 100% renewable clean energy and says lawmakers must protect air, water, and land for future generations. Introduced the Toxic PFAS Control Act to ban PFAS manufacturing and protect drinking water.
energy.short: Advocates 100% renewable energy; proposes PFAS drinking-water ban.

guns.summary: Calls gun violence a public health crisis. Supports universal background checks (championed H.R. 8), keeping weapons of war from civilians, and extreme risk protection orders; released a gun violence prevention legislative package in June 2025.
guns.short: Supports universal background checks, extreme risk orders; calls crisis.

economy.summary: Says she will fight inflationary spending, support small businesses, and make it easier for families to get ahead.
economy.short: Proposes fighting inflationary spending, supporting small businesses and families.

taxes.summary: Her platform includes reducing the tax burden on homeowners and protecting seniors from being forced out of their homes; she describes her approach as limited government and personal responsibility.
taxes.short: Supports reducing homeowner taxes, protecting seniors, limited government.

education.summary: Supports strong, community-centered education. Says civics education on the Constitution and citizenship should be foundational, and supports faith-based character formation and programs serving children with special needs.
education.short: Supports community-centered schools, foundational civics, faith-based character education.

energy.summary: Opposes the proposed Pennsylvania American Water and Essential Utilities merger, saying it benefits data centers over families, and criticizes state data-center legislation for removing public appeal rights and transparency.
energy.short: Opposes water utility merger she says favors data centers.

guns.summary: Says she will back law enforcement, prosecute violent crime, and protect neighborhoods and local schools; also emphasizes combating human trafficking and AI-enabled exploitation of children.
guns.short: Proposes backing law enforcement, prosecuting violent crime, protecting schools.
